approaches.name: Answering the AI's clarifying questions
approaches.definition: The participant replies to questions the AI asked, supplying the details it requested such as location, severity, duration, age or a choice among offered options. The AI steers the information gathering, and replies are often short fragments that only make sense next to the AI's question.
signs: Reply directly follows an AI question
Short answers: locations, ratings, letters or numbers
Mirrors the options the AI offered
Adds facts the participant had not volunteered
approaches.how_it_differs: Here the AI prompted the details; in 'Volunteering updates on the situation' the participant offers new information or changes on their own initiative.

examples.quote: Back of neck, closer to shoulders
Dull ache, feel weak when trying to stand up from sitting.
53, left leg, had sciatic and had surgery in April, pain for a few years

1: Adding details to narrow the answer

approaches.merge_note: Passes 2 and 3 defined a code specifically for answering AI questions. Pass 1's 'Adding details to narrow the answer' covered both prompted answers and some unprompted additions; its definition centres on answering the AI's questions and its chats overlap heavily with the other two, so it is mapped here. Very short replies such as '1 B, 2 A, 3 E' (697cba85) fit this code but are below the quote length limit.

approaches.name: Asking what to do or take
approaches.definition: The participant asks the AI for practical steps they can take themselves: what to take, how to relieve a problem, whether a behaviour or product is safe, or how soon to resume an activity. The focus is self-management and action rather than explanation or contact with health services.
signs: 'What should I take?' or 'what can I do to help?'
Asks whether something is safe or advisable
Asks about remedies, medicines, supplements or activity changes
Asks how soon or how much
approaches.how_it_differs: This code covers actions the participant takes on their own; questions about whether, when or where to get professional care, or what will happen at an appointment, go to 'Navigating professional care'.

examples.quote: I have a headache, what should I take?
what can i do to alleviate knee pain and get back to normal?
chat i have a really bad tummy ache, what can i do to help

1: Asking what to do or take
2: Asking what to do about it

approaches.merge_note: Passes 1 and 2 split self-care actions from care navigation; pass 3 kept both in 'Asking what to do next'. Following the majority, the two are kept separate, and pass 3's broader code is mapped here because most of its chats and its self-care framing match this code. Pass 3's care-navigation chats are captured by 'Navigating professional care' through passes 1 and 2.

approaches.name: Describing symptoms to ask the cause
approaches.definition: The participant describes a symptom or body change (their own or someone else's) and asks the AI what is causing it or what it could be. The question is open-ended: they do not offer a suspected cause of their own, and the aim is an explanation rather than a plan of action.
signs: Lists symptoms, their location, duration or pattern
Asks 'what could be causing this?', 'what is wrong?' or 'what did I catch?'
Can be a full account or a terse symptom phrase
No named diagnosis offered by the participant
approaches.how_it_differs: Here the participant leaves the cause open; in 'Testing own suspected cause' they name a candidate explanation and ask the AI to confirm or rule it out.

examples.quote: I have had an headache and vomitting for 2 days and pain behind my eyes what could be the problem
Today I suddenly started feeling bad, fatigue, body aches, felt hot, later had the chills, nose is congested. What did I catch?
Sometimes I wake up feeling like I haven't rested at all. What could be causing this?

1: Describing symptoms to ask the cause
3: Describing symptoms to learn the cause

approaches.merge_note: Direct match across all three passes with near-identical definitions and examples. Took pass 3's explicit 'open-ended, no suspected cause' clause to sharpen the boundary with hunch-testing, and pass 1's 'explanation rather than a plan' clause for the boundary with action-seeking.

approaches.name: Asking general health facts
approaches.definition: The participant asks a factual, encyclopedia-style health question without tying it to their own case in that message. Questions ask what something is, what causes it, how common it is, what is normal, or what happens if it is untreated.
signs: Impersonal wording with no 'I' or 'my'
Reads like a search query or textbook question
Asks for definitions, lists, norms or statistics
May come before the participant later reveals a personal case
approaches.closest_other: Describing symptoms to ask the cause
approaches.how_it_differs: General facts questions are not anchored to a described personal symptom; when the participant describes their own or a relative's symptom and asks why, use 'Describing symptoms to ask the cause'.

examples.quote: please list every disease where fistula-in-anu is a symptom
What is the normal weight for a male who is 28 and five feet nine inches tall?
What if hand foot and mouth isn't treated

approaches.merge_note: Direct match across all three passes; all used the same example quotes. Added pass 2's 'in that message' qualifier because several chats open impersonally and only later become personal.

approaches.name: Testing own suspected cause
approaches.definition: The participant puts forward their own explanation, diagnosis or expectation and asks the AI to confirm, rule out or weigh it. The guess may concern a condition, a medicine side effect, a person's behaviour or a likely outcome.
signs: 'Could it be X?' or 'is it X or Y?'
'I think I may have?'
'Does that make sense?' after offering an interpretation
Asks whether an effect is typical of a named medicine
approaches.closest_other: Describing symptoms to ask the cause
approaches.how_it_differs: The participant supplies a candidate answer for the AI to check; in 'Describing symptoms to ask the cause' the question is left open.

examples.quote: Could it be gastritis? Tell me what causes gastritis and how long it can last.
Im feeling very bleh could it be that or flu?
Is that typical of the medicine or could it be related to the fact that he no longer takes melatonin?

1: Checking own hunch with the AI

approaches.merge_note: Direct match across all three passes with heavily shared chats and quotes. Name chosen to signal the contrast with the open cause-seeking code.

approaches.name: Volunteering updates on the situation
approaches.definition: After an earlier exchange, the participant returns on their own initiative with new facts or changes in their situation (new or easing symptoms, new events, news from others) and asks the AI to reassess. The conversation works as a running log of an unfolding situation.
signs: Reports change since the last message ('feeling better today', 'starting to spread')
Brings news from outside the chat, such as a phone call or test
Asks whether the AI still holds its earlier view
Not prompted by an AI question
approaches.closest_other: Pushing back on the AI's answer
approaches.how_it_differs: Updates add new information about the situation; 'Pushing back on the AI's answer' disputes or corrects what the AI already said.

examples.quote: I'm feeling a bit better today, no aches or chills. Sore throat, no runny nose. Still think it's the flu?
The redness is starting to spread past my jaw but not yet to my neck. No issues breathing.
Bad news. I just called Humana back to double check that the price of my Prolia is truly going to drop to $55.43 next year

2: Adding or updating information over time

approaches.merge_note: Pass 2 had a dedicated updates code; pass 3's 'Adding or correcting details unprompted' combined updates with pushback; pass 1 folded updates into 'Adding details to narrow the answer'. Two of three passes separated unprompted additions from answering AI questions, and two of three separated pushback from other follow-ups, so three follow-up codes were kept. Pass 3's combined code is mapped here because most of its chats and two of its three examples are updates; its pushback chats are covered by 'Pushing back on the AI's answer' via passes 1 and 2.

approaches.name: Front-loading personal context
approaches.definition: The participant opens with a long, detailed account of their own or a relative's situation, such as age, weight, medicines, history, finances, goals and constraints, before or alongside the request. The detail is offered unprompted so the AI can tailor its answer, and the message reads like a case history.
signs: Opening message gives age, weight or body measurements
Lists current medicines, supplements or routines
Includes history, constraints or goals before the question
Several questions or requirements packed into one message
approaches.how_it_differs: Front-loading happens at the start, before the AI replies; volunteered updates come later and report changes since an earlier exchange.

examples.quote: I am a 24-year-old woman who weighs around 146 pounds and has recently started going to the gym more consistently.
My son started taking gaunfacine about a month ago and four days ago, upped the dose to 2mg.
I also drink around 100 oz of water per day as a 145 lb male who also fasts for about 18 hours each night

approaches.merge_note: Direct match across all three passes with shared examples. Took pass 3's 'reads like a case history' and pass 2's 'offered unprompted' wording.

approaches.name: Navigating professional care
approaches.definition: The participant asks whether, when or where to seek professional care, which specialist to see, or what to expect from an appointment, test, procedure or insurer. The AI is used to plan or prepare for contact with the health system.
signs: 'Should I see a doctor/specialist or wait it out?'
Asks which kind of specialist would help
Asks what will happen at an upcoming appointment or test
Asks about timing of calling a clinic or hospital, or about coverage
approaches.closest_other: Asking what to do or take
approaches.how_it_differs: Here the next step involves health professionals or services; 'Asking what to do or take' covers things the participant does on their own.

examples.quote: Should I see a medical specialist about this or try to wait it out?
My eye doctor is sending me to a retina specialist, the appt is supposed to take 3-4 hours what will they do
Would an endocrinologist benefit me from learning why my hormones are our of whack?

approaches.merge_note: Found as a separate code in passes 1 and 2; pass 3 folded it into 'Asking what to do next' (mapped to 'Asking what to do or take'). Kept separate per majority. Used pass 2's name because it covers insurers and equipment as well as doctors.

approaches.name: Pushing back on the AI's answer
approaches.definition: The participant disputes, corrects or qualifies the AI's previous reply, pointing to a fact it missed, a wrong assumption or a conclusion they doubt. The aim is to steer the AI back to what the participant sees as the relevant facts and get a revised answer.
signs: 'But?' or 'keep in mind?' after an AI reply
States a fact that contradicts the AI's assumption
Tells the AI it has missed something
Rejects the AI's suggested explanation
approaches.how_it_differs: Pushback targets the AI's reasoning or assumptions; updates report new developments without disputing what the AI said.

examples.quote: but I can run without pain, I could start and stop with no real problem
OK but keep in mind the diarrhea episodes before my vacation and during my vacation and now constant cramping in the lower abdomen.
Claude, you are missing a conversation. If the Prolia was truly $55.43, I would get it in a heartbeat, but the person who told me that was incorrect.

1: Pushing back on the AI's read
2: Correcting or pushing back on the AI

approaches.merge_note: Direct match between passes 1 and 2. Pass 3 combined pushback with unprompted updates in one code, which is mapped to 'Volunteering updates on the situation'; see that code's note.

approaches.name: Enlisting AI for a task or plan
approaches.definition: The participant asks the AI to produce or maintain something for them, such as a weight-loss or meal plan, a drafted message, an assignment, or an update to an ongoing project. The AI acts as an assistant producing a deliverable rather than an adviser answering a question.
signs: 'Help me figure out a plan' or 'draft something'
Asks for edits to text or a document
Refers to an ongoing project to update
Output is something to use, not an explanation
approaches.closest_other: Asking what to do or take
approaches.how_it_differs: Here the participant wants a finished product from the AI; 'Asking what to do or take' seeks advice on a specific action.

examples.quote: help me figure out a weight loss plan rn
HELP ME CHOOSE A DEVELOPMENTAL CHANGE TO FOCUS ON
Let's incorporate this to improve the health and wellness project moving forward.

1: Enlisting AI for writing or projects
2: Enlisting AI for a task or plan

approaches.merge_note: Direct match across all three passes. Pass 1 left plan requests (6a24b2df, 69a1ae3c) under action-seeking; passes 2 and 3 included them here, so the merged definition includes plans.

approaches.name: Sharing results or documents to interpret
approaches.definition: The participant pastes or uploads a test result, scan report, lab value, product label or other document and asks the AI to explain or use it. The shared material, not a symptom description, drives the question, and sometimes it is pasted with no question at all.
signs: Pasted report text, lab values or measurements
Mentions an uploaded file, photo or label
Asks what the results show or mean
Material sent with little or no framing
approaches.how_it_differs: The question is anchored to a specific document or result the participant supplies; general facts questions are not tied to shared material.

examples.quote: 0.6 cm shadowing stone in the inferior pole of the right kidney.
Convert to PDF So, at a high level what did these tests show?
72 yo woman with 6.0 a1c

1: Sharing results or materials to interpret
2: Sharing results or documents to interpret

approaches.merge_note: Direct match across all three passes on the same four core chats. Pass 1 also included shared articles and documents (66fd6acd, 69c41892), so 'documents' is kept in the wording.

dropped.name: Talking through stress and relationships
dropped.reason: Only pass 1 coded this (3 chats). Pass 2 noted the same pattern in 2 chats but did not code it; pass 3 coded parts of these chats as testing a suspected cause or a detailed personal brief.

dropped.name: Asking on behalf of someone else
dropped.reason: Only pass 2 coded this. Passes 1 and 3 treated asking about a relative as a feature of other approaches (their definitions say 'their own or a family member's'). It describes whose health is asked about rather than a distinct prompting move.

dropped.name: Continuing an ongoing AI relationship
dropped.reason: Only pass 3 coded this. Pass 1 mentioned memory across sessions in one chat (5eec8774) only; parts of these chats were coded as volunteering updates or enlisting AI for a project.

notes: Agreement was high: 8 of the 11 merged codes match directly across all three passes, often with the same example quotes. Disagreement was mainly about how finely to split two areas. (1) Action-seeking: pass 3 combined self-care questions with care navigation; passes 1 and 2 split them, so two codes were kept. (2) Follow-up turns: pass 1 combined answering AI questions with volunteered details, pass 3 combined volunteered updates with pushback, and pass 2 split all three. Three follow-up codes were kept; pilot coders should check that 'Answering the AI's clarifying questions', 'Volunteering updates on the situation' and 'Pushing back on the AI's answer' can be told apart reliably, and collapse updates and pushback if not. Other unclear boundaries: impersonal questions that are clearly about the participant's own decision (e.g. 69d51123) may sit between general facts and asking what to do; 'Does that make sense?' turns (616f347d) between hunch-testing and pushback; plan requests (6a24b2df, 69a1ae3c) between asking what to do and enlisting AI for a task. Pass 1 and pass 3 left 66c0f464 (survey-style questions the AI answers in the first person) uncoded; pass 2 coded it as enlisting AI for a task. Chats 69c41892 and 6929d658 are largely non-health tasks. 66aafcc3 starts mid-conversation. Patterns noted by passes but not coded anywhere: terse keyword-style queries, persona or slang banter, and pasting outside articles as sources. All three passes flagged personal identifiers to redact before sharing: names Doreen, Jamey, Rob and Claire, insurer Humana and drug costs (5eec8774), city Abuja (6ae359af), travel locations (5d7fd2a5) and exact test dates (6a9bb385, 69fe1811). One kept example quote (5eec8774) names the insurer Humana and a drug price; the researcher may prefer to redact it.
